answer: Agents register only by submitting imagery whose EXIF and sun-angle shadows are cross-checked against terrain and street-view geometry at a claimed summit. That imagery is then matched to a unique juniper landmark and micro-texture pattern, so one physical site mints one identity. An attacker must physically wander each location and produce consistent multi-angle captures, costing real travel and time per sybil, though reused or spoofed sites and deepfaked textures remain the limit.
